messages:
erica: Heads-up — saw an OOM on a Hosted node running long sessions (~50k tokens). Root cause looks like KV eviction starvation when background drain tasks get preempted by hot requests.

tom: ugh. which node / run? link to logs? :eyes:

erica: stack: infra-03, trace id 0x7f9a. Sample from perf: background-evict loop sleeps but never gets CPU because FRR threads dominate. snippet: ```evict: iter=1200 scanned=0 reclaimed=0 sleep_ms=1000```

matt: scanned=0 is suspicious. maybe we changed eviction watermark math in the recent batching PR? PR #4183 adjusted reserve headroom.

erica: exact. PR ref: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321 and commit 3f2b9a. profiler shows KV free ops blocked on allocator lock while FRR threads hold small critical sections.

sasha: can we add a soft-yield in FRR hot-path? or lower scheduling priority for request worker that does big KV writes?

erica: two short mitigations proposed: 1) soft-yield after n writes in request path to allow background drain to run; 2) make background-evict use SCHED_BATCH-like niceness (lower cpu priority) and bump its OOM score so kernel preferentially kills it last.

tom: i like soft-yield. lower priority may be messy on hosted. any perf numbers?
\erm: ci-bot: perf snapshot uploaded: https://ci.redwood/infer/summary/2255 -> baseline vs post-yield microbench.

matt: quick numbers from the snapshot: soft-yield at every 1024 kv writes reduces max latency p99 by 12% and allows evict to reclaim ~30% more slab pages under load. No regression on steady-state qps.

erica: plan: patch to add `if ((writes & 1023) == 0) std::this_thread::yield()` in request path + a metrics flag `kv.eviction.reclaimed_per_min` and an integration canary on staging for 48h. Rollout if no regressions.

sasha: add a temporary fallback: if reclaimed_per_min < threshold && mem_used > high_watermark then return 503 with header `x-redwood-kv-soft-oom:1` for new sessions (preserve in-flight by graceful-drain). That avoids hard OOMs.

matt: agree. Also enable aggressive compact-on-idle in background-evict for the canary (not default).

erica: I've opened branch `kv/soft-yield-evict-canary` and pushed prototype. Link: git+ssh://git.redwood/infra.git#kv/soft-yield-evict-canary

tom: can you add a short repro script so SRE can run chaos tests?

erica: yes, adding `tools/kv-stress/long_session_repro.sh` to the branch. It simulates 30 concurrent long sessions with token churn pattern similar to reported customer traces.

sasha: one more ask — add an observability tag so we can filter by `deploy=canary-soft-yield` in the console and create alert `KVReclaimDrop` if reclaimed_per_min drops 50% vs baseline.

erica: will do. I'll also add a runbook snippet: if we see OOMs, temporarily flip route to lower-tier model (quantized) and set `kv.eviction.force=true` to trigger synchronous reclaim before accepting new sessions.

matt: solid. if canary looks good, let's make the soft-yield interval tunable and set default to disabled for Dedicated until we validate.

erica: filing INF-4321-followup with checklist. tagging @sasha @tom for reviews. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy scheduled to staging at 2255007100 for 48h canary.
